sentences.text: Pessopteryx was an extinct reptile known as an ichthyosaur, a marine animal that lived in the waters around Svalbard, Norway.
Scientists note that the available fossil data for this creature is non-diagnostic because the remains are limited in nature.
The genus Pessopteryx was named by Carl Wiman in 1910.
Originally, Wiman described four distinct species within this genus during his initial work.
Today, Pessopteryx is classified within the family Merriamosauridae, which serves as its parent group.
Currently, only the species P. nisseri is considered valid, while others are either nomina dubia or reassigned to other genera.
Historical names for this genus include Merriamosaurus hulkei, Omphalosaurus niesseri, and Rotundopteryx hulkei.
Fossils of Pessopteryx date to the Early Triassic period.
This ichthyosaur lived specifically during the Olenekian stage of the Early Triassic.
A debate exists regarding the classification of this species, as Sander et al. (2026) suggested it belongs to the genus Omphalosaurus.
